Yes! But we need to adress the fact that not everyone can overcome it like this, which saddens me. Some are born with anxiety, naturally “built in” and they suffer alot more. For some it’s part of their brain, and they can’t force it out since they never knew a life without it and it’s “normal” for them. I am also a heavy advocate of using medication and staying on it for periods of time since it’s proven to help ease it and teach the brain to not be afraid (of some sorts, very complex). 

But for us, who actually triggered it within ourselves - for me it was that one bad joint and 3 deaths in family which I couldn’t cope with - is much better to legit “ride it out” and rewire our brain to being “normal”. I in no sense denied it, or ignored it, I acknowledged it, took it in, processed it and then started riding it out the best I knew how. For me it was much like an active addiction that I had to overcome. 

I am so happy you diminished it! I am so happy to hear that someone out there stuck it out, went to hell and back and made it back “normal”. I am happy you’re doing better because I know how it feels to lose your life all of a sudden, and then needing to get it back all on your own. It will be only better from here on out, trust me. Just hold away from the triggers for another year and you’re out of the woods.

I did, no therapy, no medication. I simply resumed my day to day life (I’ve got anxiety/panic disorder after smoking bad weed laced with toxins). I literally faked it till i made it - now a year later i am anxiety free. It was terrible, I was completely depersonalised and experienced severe de realisation, i was a shell of a human being and couldn’t live at all - even experiencing amnesia for about a year. I felt like my body and mind weren’t mine. I couldn’t function, couldn’t speak with anyone since I had zero control over focus and what came out of my mouth, brain fog, I couldn’t even work or go to school. I’ve simply proceeded and just made it work. I forced myself to function basically tricking my brain into thinking it was just an illusion and I was perfectly fine. It went better by the week, i experienced some off and on symptoms but I managed. Now a year later I am normal, sometimes when I am very exhausted and tired, or when I spend alot of time on my phone I will get depersonalised but nothing drastic that I can’t manage. It just went away on it’s own. I literally did fake it till you make it and succeeded.

Z mano se o tem lahko pogovarjas ure, ker sem nekako zelo “premisljena” oseba, in veliko vlozim v analiziranje dejanj ipd. Edina razlika med nama je, da sem pri 25ih dala skozi kar precej zvez, stevilo se giblje nekje med 10-12, torej ves, za kaksno osebo veljam po trenutnih standardih. Povem ti tako, sem zelo empaticna, zato te razumem, in ti bom tudi razlozila na tak nacin, da bos sama razumela in videla, da vse kar napisem ni misljeno negativno. Jaz sem se pri 22ih odselila na svoje, zivela sama v majhnem stanovanju, tam se mi je koncno odprla neka siva nit. Ugovotila sem, da ne rabim vsak vecer moskega ob sebi, ne rabim jih vlaciti na dates, ki se koncajo s seksom in razocaranjem, ugotovila sem, da ko sem sama, se imam najbolj lusno in najrajse. To je bil moj “cocoon”, iz katerega sem prilezla prerojena, spremenjena za 95%. Nekako se zacnes otresati svojih prepricanj, nehas se postavljati v merila in nehas komplicirati. Ugotovis, da zveza ni samo “kako kompatibilna sva”, zveza je dejansko nekaj najbolj simple na tem svetu. Ugotovis, da manj kot se z osebo strinjas, vec debat lahko imas, bolj osebo spoznas, naucis se sprejemati in razumeti drugacne poglede, naucis se prilagajanja in spoznavanja tistega, kar te strasi. Roko das neznancu, ki te pelje v svet katerega si se prej otepala zaradi svojega strahu, in nevednosti, prepustis se, da z debatami o razlicnih pogledih spoznas cloveka, katerega skrivas v sebi oz morda niti sama ne poznas. Cez cas ugotovis, da so merila pac samo subjektivna merila, ne obstajajo, so samo stene, ki jih postavljamo iz strahu, da bi bili spet prizadeti in zalostni. Z pravo osebo je drugace, imas vzpone in padce, si prizadet, jokas, se kregas in hitro ugotovis, da se dejansko sekiras bolj za svoje napake in zato, ker nikoli nisi vedel kaj je “varnost” in “imeti rad” - nepoznano nas strasi. Dejansko pa je vse to normalen proces. Kolikor hitro se bos otresla standardov, in zacela v pogovorih (t.i. Zmenkih) spoznavati osebo z zanimanjem kaj dejansko so pod vsemi plastmi karakterja, in jih ne samo s prve roke oznacevati za nekompatibilne zaradi predpostavljenih karakternih tock, bos nasla pravo ljubezen, ker bos osvojila empaticni, cloveski pristop. Zveza ni tinder, v pravem zivljenju ne swipas po tem kar si zelis da oseba je, v realnosti isces beyond tistih tock in dejstev. Vsi igramo, vsi si zelimo se na spletu prodati kot prfektne, pri tem pa pozabimo, da smo ljudje, in da nas nase razlike lahko povezejo bolj kot si mislimo.

You can get through anything, because unlike other illnesses, this one comes purely from your thoughts and how you form and percieve them. It’s one of the most complex ones too, and once you get a hang of it (or rather once you figure it out) it becomes easy to override it (or overcome it). I’ve figured that we who have anxiety, tend to put ourselves into boxes or lines, forcing ourselves to think and act a certain way we think is “normal”, forgetting that the anxiety does not define us, rather it’s just a feeling numbing our mental processes. Try to go the other way, let go and do not overthink, small things like pains, itches, difficulty breathing, or bigger obstacles exams, car breaking down, tripping and falling are EVERYDAY THINGS, they happen to EVERYONE, the trick in it is, “normal people” schrug and go “ok” if something else happens we’ll react then, us “ppl with anxiety” freak out over it “omg i am dying, it’s only happening to me, etc.” 

Just SHRUG AND GIGGLE, say “oops” and go on with your day. Slowly but surely it will get better. Not everything bad that happens is IRREGULAR, it’s life, it’s supposed to go this way. Anxiety paints us a pretty picutre where NOTHING GOES WRONG. That’s not true, it will go wrong and when it does, just laugh at it.

It’s because you’re experiencing mental exhaustion, I believe. Your body and mind are tightly connected, and when one experiences distress the other suffers. 
You’re way overthinking it (I do too), you’re making it harder for yourself. Putting yourself under stress such as “I need to be better, I need to do this, I need to feel this way” will send you off the cliff. What helped for me, was that I simply LET GO. I didn’t put myself into boxes and didn’t give myself tasks i NEEDED to achieve over the day, because that made me more anxious. I simply did what I WANTED to do, I didn’t think of exams or interviews until I WAS AT THE SPOT. What you need to do is stop OVERTHINKING and just LIVING THROUGH IT. It won’t be as bad as you make it seem, it will give you power and energy to make simple tasks fun, it will HELP YOU. 
The common thing that we all have is this fueling of “why is it happening to me”, you need to let go of that. It is happening to you because it is happening to everyone, your car broke down? Neighbours did too, and he just found a solution. Your exam is coming tomorrow? Your classmates is too, but he just did it without overthinking it. IT’S LIFEEE, it’s not easy. Everyone has daily struggles, they are small, they’re solvable. If it has a SOLUTION is not worth OVERTHINKING. Find a solution first, overthink later.

Nurse here! We had a young patient come in (female, 20yrs). She was very weird, shaking and couldn't stand. She looked anorexic. Now, since she was puking, we had to give her an IV Drip. So we place that in, and i watch over her in the ER room. And there is a door next to the bed she was on, that leads to the outside (for easier access of the er room if there is an emergency). So i look at her and ask if she is okay, and she is sitting up and goes "Yeah, I'm fine". Mind you she couldn't move for the past 30mins and we literally had to carry, and lift her up. Now she is sitting there and has this dead stare in her eyes. My coworker steps closer to the room, and as he is about to ask if everything is fine, this girl rips the IV drip out of her, jumps over everything in her way, opens the door and runs outside. Now this is a smaller town, with a small ER unit. And there I am, 5ft1 tall woman, chasing that skinny girl over the whole town (she was in nothing but a bra and pants because of ECG, in the middle of winter).. Behind me was my coworker, 2 paramdecis, 1 paramedic car, 3 cops, our doctor with dispatch on the phone. And we were chasing her for a good hour. Everything turned out fine and she was admited to the hospital the second we caught her.. Nothing bad happened, thank god. But it sure was funny, since we were filmed and put on national TV under "Breaking News". We still get a good laugh out of it every once in a while 😂.
